241.canonical: Use DNS as the first and simplest layer of load balancing, but treat it as insufficient on its own because it depends on client cooperation to expire and refetch records and gives weak control over client behaviour (the authoritative server sees the recursive resolver, not the user).

244.canonical: Terminate TCP/TLS at a Layer 7 reverse-proxy or edge front end as close to the user as possible — keeping long-lived, pre-warmed encrypted connections to backends — to minimise handshake round-trip latency and to absorb low-level attacks (e.g. SYN floods) and slow-client buffering that backend termination cannot handle.

245.canonical: Health-check backends and give each an explicit 'lame-duck' state in which it keeps serving in-flight requests but asks clients to stop sending new ones (propagated to active and, via periodic health checks, inactive clients), so backends can be drained, removed, or updated without disrupting user requests.
